incumbent_reading: The paper holds that financial performance did not determine how distributors identified, and reports that clear net-profit figures could not be had from them.

wager.statement: This unit speaks in one fragment, so the retelling is short. Asked for their net profit, current and former distributors did two things: they did not produce a clear figure, and they disagreed among themselves about which product margins and which training expenses belong in the sum (F23). The paper takes this as a limit on what could be measured and goes on to conclude that money did not sort people (C09). Told from the distributors' side it is a report about them. Among the people doing this work, what the business earns is not a settled number; it depends on what one is prepared to call a cost. The cost in dispute is not a small one. Distributors paid for their training (F11), and the training is printed as a system of books, recordings, meetings, rallies and seminars (F10); books and tapes are also among the media through which members met model dreams (F35). Whoever leaves those expenses out has a business that nets more than whoever puts them in. The wager is that the disagreement in F23 ran between those who stood with [6 words of Pratt (2000), p. 462], and that counting the training as a cost of the business, or not counting it, is itself a way of standing toward the organization. If that is so, financial result cannot be laid beside identification as a separate measure, as F22 lays it, since a distributor's own figure already holds an answer to what the training is. This does not dispute that money failed to sort people; it disputes that money was a separate thing to sort them by. The stub does not say along what line the disagreement ran, and it leaves 'could not' and 'would not' unseparated.

what_it_would_take_to_cohere.observation: Each distributor's own reckoning, what they counted and what they left out, set beside whether they were current or former; and, for those who gave no figure, whether it was unknown to them or kept back.
what_it_would_take_to_cohere.basis: Absent. F23 is the only fragment in which this unit speaks, and it reports the disagreement without saying who held which view. The fragments around it give sales levels (F22) and Amway's own figures for activity and gross earnings (F24, F25), not anyone's reckoning. The audit's absence register lists comparable net figures as not ascertainable; the reading asks who counted what, and claims nothing about the figures themselves.

strains_against: F22 -- the observation that high sellers quit and low earners stayed favorable rests on sales levels, which the dispute over costs does not touch; on that measure money still fails to sort people, whatever line the disagreement ran along.

F24 -- Amway's own publication gives the share of active distributors and of those reaching a sales volume, and F25 a typical gross figure; these are measures of financial result that no one's stance can alter.
F23 -- the stub reports current and former distributors together and gives no sign that the two differed, and that they differed is the whole of the wager.
wager.who_could_complete_it: Interview material in which a distributor's own account of margins and training expenses can be matched to that distributor's standing as current or former.

fragment_jobs.F23: is the unit's only speech: distributors gave no clear net figure and disagreed about what to count, and the reading takes the disagreement as the finding.
fragment_jobs.F11: prints that distributors themselves paid for training, so the disputed expense is one they bore.
fragment_jobs.F10: prints what the training was, a system of books, recordings, meetings, rallies and seminars, which gives the disputed expense its content.
fragment_jobs.F35: prints books and tapes among the media through which members met model dreams, which ties the disputed expense to the practice the paper calls dream building.
fragment_jobs.F22: is where the paper lays financial result beside reactions to Amway, in terms of sales levels and financial success, not the net figures F23 says were missing.

grounded_in.question: Along what line did the disagreement over margins and training expenses run: between current and former distributors, or across both?
grounded_in.if_one_way: If former distributors counted the training as a cost and current ones did not, C09 would read differently: a distributor's financial result would be partly made by where they stood toward Amway and could not be the separate quantity that fails to determine identification.
grounded_in.if_the_other: If the disagreement cut across current and former alike, C09 would read as the paper has it, with F23 a caveat about measurement and no more.

grounded_in.question: Of those who gave no clear figure, which could not and which would not?
grounded_in.if_one_way: If they could not, distributors were themselves without a net figure, and C09 would read as close to given: money could hardly sort people who did not know their own result.
grounded_in.if_the_other: If they would not, a figure existed and was kept from the researcher, and C09 would read as untested on net result, with sales level (F22) standing in for it.

grounded_in.how: F22 sorts distributors by sales level and financial success; F23 says the net figures were not given and that distributors disagreed on how to reckon them. One speaks as if financial result were known, the other says it was not.

rival: The disagreement is ordinary uncertainty about how to keep the books of a business that distributors often ran part time (F11), and it carries no information about where anyone stood. F23 is the caveat about measurement the paper takes it to be, and C09 rests well enough on sales levels (F22) and on Amway's own figures (F24, F25).

verdicts.note: KILL. The statement asserts: "The cost in dispute is not a small one." No fragment carries this assertion about the magnitude of the disputed training expense. F11 establishes that distributors paid training costs; F10 describes the training media and activities; F23 establishes disagreement about which expenses to count; F35 establishes that books and tapes conveyed model dreams. None establishes the amount, relative burden, or financial significance of the disputed expense. A list of training activities does not establish a large expenditure. F25 supplies only an estimate of typical gross earnings, and F64 reports an upline comparison with the capital requirements of other businesses; neither supplies the missing magnitude. The reading imports financial size when moving from the existence and breadth of training to the claim that its disputed cost was substantial. No author-account-to-event drift was identified.

considered_not_fired.item: F23: the opening account and its fragment job
considered_not_fired.why: The absence of clear net-profit figures, disagreement over product margins and training expenses, and the unresolved distinction between inability and unwillingness are all carried by F23. "Asked for their net profit" is an ordinary paraphrase of this interview report, not an added motive or cause. The statement that earnings are not a settled number is supported as a description of the disputed reckoning, not as proof that every individual lacked a private figure.

considered_not_fired.item: "This unit speaks in one fragment" and "is the unit's only speech"
considered_not_fired.why: F23 is the only fragment assigned the combined unit "current and former distributors." On that explicit unit-level reading, the assertion is supported. Individual current, inactive, and former distributors also speak elsewhere, so this does not establish that F23 exhausts all distributor testimony.

considered_not_fired.item: F11, F10, and F35: the training clauses and fragment jobs
considered_not_fired.why: F11 carries distributors paying training costs, so describing the expense as one they bore adds no causal fact. F10 carries books, recordings, meetings, rallies, and seminars as training activities. F35 carries books and tapes as media for model dreams. Connecting training and dream building through those shared media is supported; it does not document the size of the expense or any individual's actual accounting choices.

considered_not_fired.item: F22, F23, and C09: the paper's treatment of financial performance
considered_not_fired.why: F22 carries high sales before quitting and favorable reactions despite limited financial success; F23 carries the net-profit measurement problem. C09 explicitly states the author's conclusion about financial performance and identification. The card attributes that conclusion to the paper and uses F22 as a comparison of performance and reactions; it does not put the author's explanation into participants' mouths.

considered_not_fired.item: "Whoever leaves those expenses out has a business that nets more than whoever puts them in."
considered_not_fired.why: In the surrounding discussion of what goes into a calculation, this expresses the arithmetic effect of including or excluding an expense from the same reckoning. It requires no additional event or motive. It does not provide evidence that one actual distributor earned more than another, whose revenues and other costs could differ.

considered_not_fired.item: The proposed alignment between cost-counting and organizational stance, and the "If that is so ... since" connective
considered_not_fired.why: The card expressly labels the alignment a wager, conditions the inseparability argument on it, and states that F23 does not identify the line of disagreement. The requested person-level matching is explicitly unprinted. This is an acknowledged hypothesis and its conditional implication, not an assertion that the alignment was observed. F23 and A01 support leaving the empirical question unresolved.

verdicts.note: CLEAR. All 125 fragment stubs and their notes were examined, together with the absence register. No eligible stub requires the proposed relationship between expense-counting and organizational stance to be false. F23 is a seed and a declared strain; F22 and F24 are declared strains, and F25 is also expressly discussed in the F24 strain entry. No remaining fragment prints the person-level accounting choices needed to contradict the wager. The unsupported expense magnitude is a B import, not an E contradiction: the corpus does not report that the disputed expense was small.

considered_not_fired.item: F22, F24, and F25: sales, activity, and gross earnings
considered_not_fired.why: Their tension with treating financial results as inseparable from identification is declared. Independently, sales levels, aggregate activity, and gross earnings can coexist with stance-related choices about net-profit expenses; these stubs do not identify anyone's treatment of training costs.

considered_not_fired.item: F90-F98 and F123: former distributors' accounts and tenure
considered_not_fired.why: Declining interest, satisfaction with another job, rejection of upline authority, resentment, and departure within a year establish varied experiences of leaving. They do not report expense-counting. The wager does not require accounting disagreement to be the sole cause of departure, or all former distributors to have the same motive.

considered_not_fired.item: F101-F105 and F110: ambivalence and changing identification
considered_not_fired.why: These stubs prevent treating current membership as proof of uniformly positive identification, but the card does not establish such a universal equivalence. They contain no accounting choices that would make its proposed alignment impossible. Changing or mixed attachment can coexist with a relationship between stance and reckoning.

considered_not_fired.item: F61, F62, F64, F97, and F103: benefits, business comparisons, and evaluations of upline support
considered_not_fired.why: Intangible support, aspirations for social access, claims about other businesses' capital requirements, and favorable or unfavorable evaluations of mentoring do not specify whether training expenses were deducted. None establishes the opposite of the proposed accounting relationship or the size of the disputed expenditure.

considered_not_fired.item: F23 and A01: missing comparable net figures and unidentified accounting positions
considered_not_fired.why: A01 records comparable net-profit and net-loss figures as not ascertainable. F23 leaves both the distribution of accounting views and inability versus unwillingness unresolved. Missing evidence cannot establish an undeclared contradiction; the card expressly identifies the missing matching information.

considered_not_fired.item: C09 and the author's explanatory accounts in F19, F21, F88, F99, and F107
considered_not_fired.why: An alternative explanation of identification or a challenge to financial performance as a separate measure is not itself a contradiction of an observed event. These theoretical accounts do not supply a contrary observation about distributors' accounting choices, and disagreement with the incumbent's theory is not an E kill.

attack.kept: A killed reading is retained, marked. Deleting it removes the evidence that the pass functions.
